subject: Television & Streaming
title: Product Placement's Sneaky Rise
description: A micro-lesson that makes Product Placement's Sneaky Rise usable.

hook.text: When Coca-Cola cups appeared on the American Idol judges' table, it wasn't accidental.

buildup.text: As viewers skipped traditional ads, brands embedded products directly into shows.

discovery.text: Product placement revenue in television grew to over 20 billion dollars annually.

twist.text: The best product placement is invisible. When it's too obvious, audiences reject it.

climax.text: Product placement represents a shift: advertising no longer interrupts the show—it becomes part of the show's reality.

punchline.text: The best ad is the one you don't notice.

quiz.question: Why did product placement become increasingly important in television?
options: It was cheaper than regular ads
Viewers began skipping traditional commercials with DVRs and streaming
